summary: Backend-only regression verification after Iteration 11 (frontend-only bug fix: dashboard 'unpaid invoices' and 'overdue invoices' stat cards wrapped in TouchableOpacity so users can tap and navigate to filtered invoices). Backend has ZERO changes; the goal was to confirm no regressions and that the endpoints the new tappable cards depend on still work correctly. Ran full pytest suite: 51/51 PASSED in 12.46s. Additionally spot-checked the exact APIs the fix relies on: (1) GET /api/invoices?status=unpaid returns only invoices with status='unpaid' (8 rows, all with is_overdue field present for client-side filtering). (2) GET /api/invoices?status=partial returns only status='partial' (3 rows). (3) GET /api/invoices (no filter) returns is_overdue on every item so the frontend can do the client-side is_overdue=true filter for the overdue card. (4) GET /api/stats/dashboard still returns unpaid_invoices=11 (unpaid+partial) and overdue_count=0 as documented. No backend regressions.

minor.issue: The status query param is a free-form string; there is no whitelist (unpaid|partial|paid). An invalid value silently returns [] instead of 400. Non-blocking.

is_overdue is derived on every list call by scanning all matching invoices and updating them one-by-one (N mongo update_one calls per request). For a large invoice set this is O(N) writes on every read; consider a scheduled job or a single update_many({status:{$in:[unpaid,partial]}, due_date:{$lt:now}}, {$set:{is_overdue:true}}). Carried-over.
expense_type still a free-form string (no enum). Carried.

action_items: None required for this iteration - backend was not modified and no regressions were found.
(non-blocking, carried) Whitelist status values on GET /api/invoices (return 400 on invalid).
(non-blocking, carried) Optimize is_overdue update in GET /api/invoices to a single update_many, or move to a scheduled task.
(non-blocking, carried) Make expense_type an Enum; validate amount>0 on POST /api/expenses and POST /api/invoices/{id}/payment.
(non-blocking, carried) Wrap DELETE /api/customers/{id} cascade in a MongoDB transaction; make invoice_number generation atomic (findOneAndUpdate on a counters doc).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L399-425: GET /api/invoices?status=unpaid works correctly for the new frontend fix (filter by exact status string). is_overdue is added to every returned item, so the frontend's client-side is_overdue=true filter for the 'overdue' card will work.
server.py L417-423: On every list request, invoices past due_date get individually updated with update_one. This is correct but inefficient; prefer update_many once, then read. Carried.

server.py L666-729: /stats/dashboard.unpaid_invoices counts {status:{$in:[unpaid,partial]}} while the new frontend card navigates to /invoices?status=unpaid (unpaid only). This is intentional per the fix (11 vs 8 in my sample), but E1 should confirm the UX expectation: does the badge count include partial while the drill-down excludes it? If so, add a small note in the UI, or change the drill-down to open with a combined filter.
